# `<ptfkit/kalumba2021.h>`

```c
#include <ptfkit/kalumba2021.h>
```

Kalumba et al. (2021) PTFs for Zambezi River Basin soil hydraulic properties.

## Source

Kalumba, M., Bamps, B., Nyambe, I., Dondeyne, S., & Van Orshoven, J. (2021). Development and functional evaluation of pedotransfer functions for soil hydraulic properties for the Zambezi River Basin. European Journal of Soil Science, 72(4), 1559-1574.

[DOI: 10.1111/ejss.13077](https://doi.org/10.1111/ejss.13077)

## Scope

**Territory:** Zambezi River Basin, with field measurements from the Upper Mulungushi sub-basin.

**Dataset:** 631 soil samples: 329 Africa Soil Profiles observations and 302 Upper Mulungushi observations; target-specific sample availability is documented below.

[PTF catalog page](../../../ptf-catalog/sources/kalumba2021.md)

## Functions

### `calc_ptf_kalumba2021_mlr_pf00` {#function-calc_ptf_kalumba2021_mlr_pf00}

Estimate volumetric water content at pf 0.0 with the Kalumba et al. MLR PTF.

```c
static inline double calc_ptf_kalumba2021_mlr_pf00(double elevation, double sand, double silt, double stoniness, double nitrogen, double electrical_conductivity, double ph, double bulk_density);
```

#### Parameters

| Name | Direction | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `elevation` | in | Topographic elevation of the soil profile site. (m) |
| `sand` | in | Sand fraction used as a PTF input. (fraction) |
| `silt` | in | Silt fraction used as a PTF input. (fraction) |
| `stoniness` | in | Stoniness fraction under the reviewed Table 4 scale interpretation. (fraction) |
| `nitrogen` | in | Soil nitrogen content in percentage points. (%) |
| `electrical_conductivity` | in | Soil electrical conductivity. (dS/m) |
| `ph` | in | Soil pH measured in a 1:5 soil-to-water suspension. (1) |
| `bulk_density` | in | Soil bulk density. (g/cm^3) |

#### Returns

Volumetric water content at pF 0.0. (fractions)

!!! note

    Table 4 publishes the complete MLR equation; the target dataset is 302 Upper Mulungushi observations.

!!! warning

    Developed for Zambezi River Basin soils; the Table 1 ranges are marginal and do not define a joint Cartesian applicability domain.
